_comment: Shared vectors for how a floating panel is held to the viewport (CoreOverlayFit).
Read by coui_core (availableExtent and fit), coui_flutter (the popover engine's
height cap and where it places an over-tall panel) and a real-Chrome probe of the
Web panel CSS, so a change on one platform fails the other.
All lengths are along one axis (the vertical one, which is the only one a list
needs), in logical px on Flutter and CSS px on the Web.
Inputs: viewport, paddingBefore and paddingAfter (what the platform's collision keeps
the panel away from), start (where the panel's near edge sits before fitting) and
extent (how far the panel extends, its natural height).
Expected: room (availableExtent) and fit: the start and extent after fitting, and whether
the panel was capped. A capped panel takes the whole room and starts at paddingBefore;
one that fits is left as it is.

cases.name: a panel that fits keeps its place and size
a panel exactly as tall as the room fits and is not capped
a panel a pixel over the room takes the room and starts at the near padding
thirty menu rows in a phone-sized viewport
the system bars take their share of the room
a short panel near the far padding is not moved
paddings that leave no room cap any panel to nothing
an empty panel is never capped
a fractional viewport gives a fractional room
no padding gives the whole viewport
an unequal pair of paddings places the cap at the near one
